subject: Hosted inference: elevated latency for SilverOak batch jobs / status notice
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@silveroak.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 19 Jul 2025 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood: elevated inference latency impacting SilverOak batch jobs (US-WEST)

Hi Samir —

We wanted to let you know we’ve observed elevated p95/p99 generation latency for hosted inference in the US-WEST region that may be affecting SilverOak’s scheduled batch scoring jobs. We’ve posted an initial status update here: https://status.redwood.com/incidents/2025-07-19-usw-latency

Impact:
- Observed p95 increase from ~450ms to ~1.8s for generation endpoints used by your batch runner between 07:40–09:00 PDT.
- A small percentage of requests saw timeouts and retries at the client layer (you may have seen increased job durations).

What we’re doing:
- Our on-call SREs are investigating a routing and autoscaling interaction that temporarily reduced available inference capacity for some pools.
- We have enabled aggressive vertical scaling on the affected pools and applied a temporary routing bypass to shift traffic while we triage.

Mitigations for you (short-term):
- If you control the batch job concurrency, lowering parallelism by ~30% will reduce retry amplification.
- Use the model_variant=v2-lowlatency (if available on your integration) to reduce per-request latency while we restore normal capacity.

We’ll follow up with more detail from Ops once we have a root cause and timeline. Really sorry for the disruption — we know how sensitive scoring pipelines are. If you want, I can schedule a short bridge with our SREs.

Attachments: ops_incident_excerpt.txt (short excerpt from runtime logs)

Thanks,
Olga Petrov
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Redwood: elevated inference latency impacting SilverOak batch jobs (US-WEST)

Hi Samir —

Quick operational update after a findings sync with our on-call:

Summary of root cause (preliminary):
- At ~07:35 PDT an autoscaling reconciliation bug caused a subset of US-WEST inference pools to report stale capacity to the routing plane. That state caused routing decisions to favor a narrower set of worker nodes which increased KV-cache eviction and per-token scheduling contention.
- The contention manifested as elevated p95/p99 token-gen latencies and some backend request timeouts.

Actions taken so far:
- Applied a routing bypass for affected pools; we also forced a full scale-up cycle that restored healthy worker distribution by ~08:55 PDT.
- We rolled a targeted worker restart to clear KV-cache pressure and validated that p95 returned to expected ranges by 09:05 PDT for the majority of traffic.

Customer-facing ETA:
- Based on current telemetry we expect normal behavior to be sustained; however our engineers will continue monitoring for 24 hours. I recommend leaving your nightly job as-is if you can tolerate a small risk window — lowering concurrency is still the safest short-term option.

Attached is an excerpt from the ops timeline that shows the scale actions and relevant log markers (ops_incident_excerpt.txt). We’ll produce a full postmortem and a mitigation plan that includes a fix to the autoscaling reconciliation logic and an additional health-check gate for routing state.

If you’d like a brief bridge with SRE leads, Jonas is on the thread and can join.

Best regards,
Olga Petrov
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

Subject: Redwood post-incident summary: US-WEST latency deviation affecting SilverOak — follow-up and credits

Hi Samir —

Thanks again for your patience while we completed the initial investigation. Below is a short post-incident summary and next steps. Full postmortem (root cause, timeline, and permanent fixes) is at: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB2cPostmortemSilverOak

Short summary:
- Incident window: 2025-07-19 07:35–09:05 PDT (US-WEST).
- Impact: transient p95/p99 generation latency elevation for a subset of requests; small fraction (<0.5%) of requests experienced retry/timeouts leading to increased job durations for scheduled batch runs.
- Root cause: autoscaling reconciliation bug that allowed stale capacity reports to influence the routing plane, causing traffic to concentrate on fewer workers and increasing KV eviction/scheduling contention.

Remediations completed:
- Immediate: routing bypass + forced scale-up + targeted worker restarts (completed 09:05 PDT).
- Short-term code fix: additional gating around routing state updates (deployed 2025-07-20 02:00 PDT).
- Medium-term: redesign of autoscaler reconciliation to reduce state staleness and add stronger health signals to routing decisions (expected release Q3 2025).

Customer impact & compensation:
- We will apply a pro-rated credit for the affected hourly window to SilverOak’s account; Marissa is preparing the credit calculation.

Attachments: customer-mitigation-checklist.pdf (suggested client-side settings to avoid retry amplification), ops_incident_excerpt.txt

If you’d like us to run a one-off replay of affected sample requests against a canary pool to validate no residual regressions, we can schedule that with Jonas.

Please let me know if anything else would help — and again, apologies for the disruption.

Warmly,
Olga Petrov
